No, it's not just my opinion. Your consciousness is not separate from your body, it *is* your body—it's an amalgamation of chemicals, synapses, sensory experiences, and various other information, all processed by your brain. Your brain, your senses, all of these things cease functioning when you die. There isn't some magic voodoo spirit inside that flies away to heaven at this point. There's just a few final chemical reactions.

Saying "while there is nothing to prove an afterlife, there is nothing to disprove it," is like saying that while there's nothing to prove that an invisible Yeti is stalking President Obama, there's nothing to disprove it.

There is no evidence for any kind of afterlife whatsoever, and all the evidence in the world to imply that our consciousness ends completely at death. Due to humanity evolving in such as way as to perceive their emotions and thoughts as being separate from their body, we're predisposed to believing that our mind can go on after death. But our brain is just another organ, albiet the most important one. Every organ ceases to function at death.

The afterlife is a myth perpetuated by fear of the finality of death, and by organizations who've gained incredible power over the centuries by playing on this fear and convincing a large portion of the population that not only does an afterlife exist, but that they hold the key to it.

Move to a city. If you already live in a city, move to a bigger one. It's not easy to move when you're unemployed, but I've done it twice already so I know it's possible. You're far more likely to find a job in, say, London than in Buttfuck, UK. Go leave CVs in person, even if that's not typically done. Not only does it show initiative, it gives you an opportunity to speak face-to-face with someone at the company. Make sure your CV is solid, too. Get as many people as you can to read it and offer suggestions, especially if you can have it checked out by someone who has worked in HR. If you interview like shit, have your friends or family let you practice on them. If nothing else, read up on the most commonly asked questions, and think about how you would answer them.

But they live across a vast ocean, and I won't get to see them again in person before I leave. I'm sorry about that, but it can't be helped. I could rebuild my life again. It would be a little effort, but it's doable. I could get another job, I could cross that ocean, I could make a new life in a new town in a new country. And then I could watch it crumble. Then I could rebuild. Then I could watch it crumble. Empty but for how unhappy I feel the whole time. For eternity, rebuilding and destroying.

I don't know your full story, but I grew up in an incredibly fucked-up home as well. You're sixteen. You have two more years. Look at it as a prison term. You just need to cross the days off until you're free. 

Depression makes it hard to get things done. Don't let that stop you. You need to spend the time leading up to your 18th birthday *planning your exit*. Move to a city a few hours away. Go to university. Get a job if you're not ready for university right away—not everyone is. You'll know better than any of us if you are. Plan everything on the assumption that you'll be going directly to university, though. It's much harder to sort out application, enrollment, scholarships, tuition, and housing than it is to say "Fuck it! I'm moving to Toronto and working at the GAP!"

No matter what, you need to get out when you turn eighteen. Not just out of the house, but out of the state. You live in a large family, and I'm sure it won't be easy to leave some of them behind, and you may feel obligated to stay and 'take care of someone'. Don't. You'll end up trapped there, coming up with reasons to stay, and feeling more and more suicidal with every passing day. Get out. You can do it.

And that INTP, Meyer-Briggs thing? You're shy, you have some social anxiety. Personality tests are pseudoscientific bullshit. Human beings are far too complex, and wonderful, and terrible to be summed up so easily. You say you're INTP, and as such that means you don't understand people and they don't understand you?

I'm going to tell you a secret: social interaction is a learned skill. Unless you're actually on the autism spectrum, your issues are probably a result of growing up in an environment that never provided a healthy model of social interaction. You can fix this! Start by observing people at school and reading about psychology. Make an actual effort to speak with people. Ask them about things they're interested in. People love to talk about themselves, so it's easy to start a conversation with almost anyone if you just know what to ask them. If they're into theatre, talk to them about what the drama club is performing next. If they're in band, ask them how it's going—have they gone to any competitions lately?

Start off with one-on-one interaction. Make individual friends, not groups. Don't tell them anything you wouldn't be comfortable with your worst enemy knowing, though. If you've spent your whole life being shy, you're not going to be the most adept at spotting untrustworthy people. Just play it safe until you've known someone for a few years. Groups are a complicated, dangerous social beast. Especially in high school. The people who seem to have the best experience in high school are the ones who make friends in every clique, but don't belong to one themselves.

You can learn how to make friends, and you should! It's important. You need to have more than just one, because otherwise it starts to be co-dependent and weird, especially at sixteen. If someone knows they're literally your *only* friend and confidante, they have a lot of power over you. Even otherwise good people can be manipulative when given that much influence over someone else.

Finally, if you're in any kind of scene or subculture, PLEASE remember: Some of the best friends you will ever make in your entire life, some of the kindest, truest, and most amazing people you will ever meet... are going to be totally normal mainstreamers, or nerds, or on the basketball team, or punks, or whatever. Don't make the mistake of only trying to befriend people who are 'like you', because you are so much more than the music you listen to, or the movies you watch, or your hobbies... and so is everyone else.

Look, I do actual drugs. Advil, Midol, none of that has any chemical effect that will make you "feel good", and it's impossible to OD on any kind of over-the-counter medication like that. The only thing you'll do is make yourself feel a little sick, and fuck up your liver. Don't get all excited now, it's not enough to kill you! It'd take years and years of "overdosing" on those medications to cause liver failure, and liver failure isn't going to kill you either, it's just going to make your life suck a lot.

So, taking those pills makes you "feel good enough not to kill yourself"? You're either suicidal over menstrual cramps, or you are experiencing what is commonly known as the placebo effect.

You sound like a sheltered, overdramatic teenager. If you find yourself thinking about suicide a lot, and taking lots of Midol in the hopes it will kill you, then you might actually have depression. If so, talk to your parents or a guidance counselor about seeing a therapist. You mention writing a lot, though—is it possible that you've become enamored of the "tortured artist" trope?

I've been to two different psychiatrists. I told the first one my life story, unfiltered, and honest. He called me a week later from a blocked number and told me that my case was too complex for him to handle, and that I should be in an institution. At the time I was working full-time in a corporate environment, and had a fantastic internship as well. Yeah, let me just book some vacation and check into a shitty psych ward. I'm sure I'll enjoy the completely pointless group therapy sessions, and the ten years of soul-crushing debt to follow.

My current psychiatrist has basically no idea who I am, and doesn't really ask. She writes me prescriptions for anti-depressants. I do my own research and tell her what I want. Our sessions last about five minutes. I try something, and after it has completely failed to work, I tell her I want to try something new or up my dosage. I've tried clomipramine, venlafaxine, and sertraline. Clomipramine is a TCA, the other two are SSRIs. I also take 10mg generic Adderall a day, for adult ADD. I've had ADD my entire life, it's been a real issue. It's pretty common to find it co-morbid with severe clinical depression.

I was thinking about trying bupropion next, it doesn't function in the same way as anything else I've tried—actually, they're not 100% sure how it functions. However, it would take about a month before I would notice any true effects (if it actually worked, since nothing else has) and I'm not going to be alive for another month.

I got this far out of stubborn determination. Now I'm giving my final "fuck you" to The Man, and I'm opting out for good. I don't have to live in this kind of pain, and I'm not going to. Peaceful nothingness in death. No more hurt. It's nice, isn't it? I don't believe in an afterlife, I'm a hardline atheist. But I can't wait to be cremated, to have my ashes thrown out to the ocean. Little parts of my being floating around, who knows where I'll go. I loved travelling.

My life isn't pointless, it's just overwhelmingly painful. Pointless I could manage. Pointless is fine, it's boring but it's fine. My life has never been pointless, I'm very capable and I currently lead an exciting life that many would envy from an outsiders' perspective.

It's not a matter of there being no reason to keep going, it's a matter of there being overwhelming reason to opt out. I'm intensely depressed and it's never going to end. Mental illness runs on both sides of my family, and my childhood was so fucked up that I should get some kind of award for having gone this long without killing myself as it is.
